arguments.conclusion: The next chairman Kevin Marsh will permanently remove the supplementary leverage ratio restriction, allowing banks to buy treasuries, which is effectively QE.
arguments.premise_synthesis: In 2020, the Federal Reserve temporarily removed the supplementary leverage ratio restriction, and banks subsequently bought US treasuries. The same action can be taken permanently under the next chairman, effectively constituting quantitative easing.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The Fed will implement effective quantitative easing by permanently removing the SLR to allow banks to absorb treasury supply, as a response to fiscal strain.
